```{r validate}
source('../provenance_helpers.R')
snapshot <- jsonlite::read_json('palette_preview/palettes.json')
assert_hash_map(snapshot$source_hashes,'../../..')
stopifnot(snapshot$all_32_interpolations_match_original,
  snapshot$shared_preview_colour_vectors_identical)
for(well in c('A3','A1')) {
  z <- jsonlite::read_json(file.path('palette_preview',paste0(well,'_validation.json')))
  stopifnot(z$all_barcodes_individual,z$full_frequencies_verified,z$geometry_unchanged)
  for(im in z$images) stopifnot(digest::digest(file=file.path('palette_preview',im$path),
    algo='sha256')==im$sha256)
}
```

These previews use **every barcode** from chloramphenicol replicate 1 and
no-antibiotic replicate 1. Band widths, barcode order, zero counts and the
extracted-read denominator are identical across palette choices. The same
barcode receives the same colour in the treatment and control within each choice.
No barcodes are combined or filtered out.

All **32 LTC palettes by Loukas Theodosiou are built directly into barbac**.
Choose one with `palette = "alger"`; no additional palette package is needed.
These use the curated fills, with selected black and near-white colours omitted.
We interpolate each selected palette end to end to obtain a colour for every
barcode. Colour identifies a barcode; neither brightness nor hue represents its
frequency. Many thin bands and neighbouring colours remain indistinguishable at
screen resolution with this many lineages.

[Open the main report with the plasma reference plots](report.html#following-the-mixture-over-time).

## All 32 available palettes

The sheet below shows the interpolated options available in barbac. The
`heatmap0`–`heatmap3` palettes are ordered ramps; their diverging shapes should
not be interpreted as low/high barcode abundance when used for barcode identity.

![All 32 LTC palettes, interpolated end to end](palette_preview/all_palettes.png)

## Use a palette with barbac

Pass the palette name directly:

```r
library(barbac)
barbac_ts_area(
  counts, min_total_count = 0, fill_missing = "zero",
  palette = "alger", show_legend = FALSE
)

names(barbac_palettes())  # list all 32 choices
```

For multiple populations, colours must be assigned over a shared set of barcode
identifiers to keep the same barcode colour across panels, as in these previews:

```r
ids <- sort(unique(c(as.character(treatment$barcode), as.character(control$barcode))))
colours <- setNames(barbac_palette("alger", length(ids)), ids)

plot_population <- function(counts) {
  local_ids <- sort(unique(as.character(counts$barcode)))
  counts$barcode <- factor(counts$barcode, levels = local_ids)
  barbac_ts_area(counts, min_total_count = 0, fill_missing = "zero",
                 palette = unname(colours[local_ids]))
}
plot_population(treatment)
plot_population(control)
```

The existing treatment/control images are retained: barbac's native palette
vectors were checked to be identical to their original colour mappings.
The R script, exact original and native palette snapshots, source hashes and numerical validation receipts are in
`palette_preview.R` and `palette_preview/`. Click a plot for its full-size image
when the accompanying folder is available.
